question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund (open-ended Category III AIF) has a NAV of INR 250 crore. The CIO wants to know the maximum permissible total exposure (long + short, after offsetting) as per SEBI prudential norms. What is the maximum permissible leverage exposure?

answer.text: Zero leverage is permitted for Cat III AIFs

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SEBI has prescribed that leverage of a Category III AIF shall not exceed 2 times of NAV. Leverage = Total exposure (Long + Short after offsetting) / NAV. Max exposure = 2 × INR 250 cr = INR 500 crore. Reported at end of day to custodian; any breach must be squared off by next working day. **The Trap:** Option A (1x) is the zero-net-leverage reading. Option B (4x) is the SIF multi-strategy cap or a made-up figure. Option D is the Cat I/II zero-leverage rule — swapped category. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D tests Cat I/II zero leverage. VIII (Equity Derivatives) covers gross vs. net exposure. XIX-E's 2x NAV cap is the distinctive Cat III lever. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** The 2x cap is continuous, not end-of-month. Report EOD leverage to custodian; on a breach, inform all investors before 10 AM next working day and square off by EOD. Size pair-trades against the cap on gross notional, net of offsetting permitted by SEBI.
